input.title: Press reigned in by House of Lords decision
input.abstract: Various aspects of the legal case between Naomi Campbell and MGN Limited are discussed. The Mirror's decision to publish details of Ms Campbell's treatment in the context of its right to put the record straight is studied. It is stated that the more intimate the aspect of private life being interfered with, the more serious must be the reasons for doing so. It is suggested that both parliament and the courts have consistently refused to extend the law of privacy beyonds its niche within the law of confidentiality.

output.reasoning: O artigo não atende aos critérios básicos de busca por palavras-chave do protocolo (métodos computacionais, lavagem de dinheiro ou crime organizado) nos campos de título, resumo ou palavras-chave dos autores.
